wipAssessment:
I checked both plans against the code instead of trusting either. I read every file in d8bfded, fede7f4 and c35fd8a, plus the domain, schemas, services, repositories, e2e support, Playwright config and route tests at 5abf1b4. The checkout was not modified. Budget numbers come from scratch builds made in the scratchpad (git archive of 5abf1b4, the fede7f4 patch applied, node_modules symlinked, ADAPTER=node vite build, then scripts/check-budgets.ts), and from the WIP build already in .svelte-kit/output.

MEASURED FACTS THAT DECIDE THE SHAPE OF THE PLAN
1. fede7f4 applies cleanly onto 5abf1b4 and passes as is. Every route passes the stricter accounting. /profile/security is 59.6 KB, the same as under the old accounting, which leaves only 0.4 KB of headroom. The largest route CSS is /design at 11.7 KB, and whole-build CSS is 19.6 KB. Under the new accounting, /setup, / and /recover/passkey are each 0.4 KB higher than the docs table says.
2. The WIP fails budgets as designed. Every per-step route fails: 63.1 KB (/onboarding/exercises) to 69.0 KB (/onboarding/schedule). /profile/security fails at 60.8 KB. Welcome passes at 58.9 KB. There are three causes:
   - each step page imports its editor statically;
   - with bundleStrategy 'split', every route node is listed in the app entry's __vite__mapDeps, which ships on every route. The entry is 3.3 KB gzip with the WIP against 2.3 KB on the base;
   - the 'grip' icon is added to the icon map, which every route ships.
3. Route count alone breaks the budget. 20 empty static stub routes (Plan 1's 11 onboarding routes plus 9 Profile routes) add 0.54 KB to every route, and /profile/security fails at 60.1 KB.
4. Param matchers cost more than the headroom. Two dynamic routes with SvelteKit 3 defineParams matchers put /profile/security at 60.1 KB (FAIL). Lean, hand-written standard-schema matchers give 59.9 KB. With no matchers it is 59.7 KB. Adding a stub onboarding layout node, a Today +page.server.ts and both dynamic routes still gives 59.7 KB. Bare stubs measure 50.8 KB for /(app)/profile/[section] and 49.1 KB for /onboarding/[[step]]. SvelteKit 3 also requires matchers in one src/params.ts that exports `params`, as standard schemas that return the value or undefined, not a boolean.
5. Conclusion: use one dynamic route for Profile editing and one for onboarding, with no matchers (unknown keys 404 from load), and load editors lazily through a registry outside universal loads. Add no new icons. Every slice pastes the /profile/security row of its budgets output.

PLAN 1 (per-step routes, onboarding first)
- Its structure cannot pass budgets: see facts 2 and 3. It also needs a temporary Partial step map that falls back to Profile, which is a hack.
- Two of its numbers are wrong:
  - It says the stricter accounting may raise /profile/security from 59.6 KB. Measured, it stays at 59.6 KB.
  - It says routes outside (app) start at 53.6 KB. A bare route outside (app) is 49.1 KB; /recover is heavier because of AuthScreen.
- Extracting budget-graph.ts would rewrite a reviewed commit, so I deferred it.
- Adopted from Plan 1:
  - serial e2e projects with resetTrainingProfile(), profileAction() and gotoHydrated();
  - a service-level guard so required steps cannot be skipped;
  - the server helpers moved to src/lib/server;
  - design-system rows kept within the current column width;
  - many of the bug fixes.

PLAN 2 (dynamic routes, Profile first)
- Right on architecture and order, but:
  - (a) its defineParams matchers fail the budget (fact 4);
  - (b) its profile-* specs are parallel *.e2e.ts files, and the serial project only arrives at onboarding-flow. Chromium and WebKit, and two local workers, would race on the one owner's goals; WebKit would see Chromium's leftovers;
  - (c) it misses the server-side skip hole;
  - (d) its goals slice (~590 lines) is underestimated: the list, empty state and sheet without reorder, drag or manage are about 650 lines;
  - (e) its body unit test locks in the 'other unit shows blank' bug;
  - (f) its weeksUntil claim is off. The function compares calendar days correctly; the real question is whose 'today' (server or device). Compute it after hydration;
  - (g) its optional sessions.exclusive change belongs to the CI-flake stack (task #14, done). Don't touch it;
  - (h) changing appRoutes samples is not needed without matchers ('sample' still matches the route and redirects).

WIP STATE AND BUGS (all confirmed by reading or running; each is folded into a slice)
Formatting, dead code and docs:
- Prettier fails on src/routes/profile-forms.server.ts, and that file is not a route.
- Dead code: the goalStatus action (status already goes through updateGoal), sectionContext, scoped(), weeksUntil, disciplineNames, editAction, and Toggle's children prop (interactive content inside a <label>).
- design-system.md re-pads the whole table: 56 lines of churn for 7 rows.

Server and flow:
- The `?/skip` action exists on every step, and advanceOnboarding never checks STEP_INFO.optional, so a crafted POST skips goals, experience or schedule.
- then=back uses indexOf (-1 falls back to welcome) instead of previousStep().
- Back on an invalid half-filled step shows and focuses the errors, then navigates away anyway.
- Edit from review walks every later step again instead of returning to review.
- A step that does not apply renders as '1 / N'.
- The progress bar marks every earlier step done (`i < index`).
- The step URL is built by string concatenation in 4 places, with eslint-disable comments.
- rememberOnboardingStep is never called. Keep it that way so GET loads stay free of side effects; resume means the furthest step advanced.

Inputs and accessibility:
- The race time and easy pace fields use inputmode=numeric (no ':' on the iPhone keypad), but parseDuration requires ':'.
- NumberField marks its unit aria-hidden. NumberField and TextArea keep the hint id in aria-describedby while the error replaces the hint, leaving a dangling IDREF.
- ChoiceGroup radios are used as 'add' actions (ExperienceEditor 'Also train something else?', BaselinesEditor 'Add a lift'). Arrow keys add every option passed.
- Radios cannot be cleared once picked, so optional single choices need a decision.
- ScheduleEditor passes errors to NumberStepper as `hint`: no aria-invalid, nothing announced.
- GoalsEditor stacks two 36 px up/down buttons whose 44 px hit areas overlap by about 8 px.
- GoalSheet never shows errors for weight class or target.
- TagInput allows 80 characters and 40 items; the injury schema allows 60 and 12.
- ProfileSummary prints raw lift keys, and its discipline dots are not aria-hidden.

Data and editors:
- Exercise preferences lose their `reason` on every save.
- bodyDraft shows a blank weight when the latest entry is in the other unit.
- 'Not focusing on it' does not round-trip.
- Injuries, commitments and races are keyed by index; lifts and experience use `${x}:${i}`. Removing a middle row moves row-local state (such as a half-typed TagInput entry) onto the wrong item.
- scheduleDraft pre-fills 4 days and 60 min.
- ScheduleDraft is exported from a component's instance script.
- specificsDraft hard-codes the running keys instead of using RUNNING_DISCIPLINES.

Tests:
- There is no test of any kind for the WIP: no unit, integration, e2e, axe or perf coverage, and no screenshots.
